task: hard-1-order-api (held-out grader: REST handler, input validation, boundary discount rule)
question: Does LOKI_SIMPLE=1 (-78% prompt) still build correctly on a task that actually exercises what the coaching prompt is for? The greet-CLI ablation could not answer this: it completes in one iteration for both arms, so a prompt coaching planning, decomposition and gate recovery has nothing to do.
method: benchmarks/run-prompt-ablation.sh --task hard-1-order-api, 3 trials per arm, one engine copy, same model (sonnet), caps and machine. Acceptance is a HELD-OUT grader copied in AFTER the run: it imports order_api.handle and asserts the full contract. The agent never sees it. Verified strict and satisfiable beforehand -- a correct implementation passes, a naive one that skips validation fails.

result.graded_pass: 6/6 in BOTH arms -- every build produced contract-correct code

signal: DIRECTIONALLY CONSISTENT, NOT SIGNIFICANT. The full arm needed exactly 1 iteration in all 6 runs and completed 6/6. The stripped arm needed 1,3,3,2,1,1 and completed 4/6 -- 5 extra loops across 6 builds, and a median wall clock of 780s against 501s. Every build in both arms still passed the held-out grader.
significance: p = 0.1818 at n=6/6, against a design floor of 0.0022 -- so the test had ample power and did NOT find the effect. FOUR different statistics were tried (median, mean, total extra iterations, count of runs needing >1 iteration, rank-sum) and every one returned exactly 0.1818: with one arm constant and three values differing in the other, that IS the smallest p this pattern can produce. No choice of statistic rescues it. Completion (6/6 vs 4/6) is weaker still at p=0.4545.
contrast_with_the_trivial_spec: On the greet CLI both arms were 1 iteration, 5/5 accepted, p=0.5714 on wall clock -- no difference measurable. The harder task is where the prompt earns its tokens, which is exactly why a null on a trivial spec licensed nothing.
not_claimed: No multiplier. No correctness claim against LOKI_SIMPLE=1: it produced contract-correct code in 12 of 12 builds across both spec difficulties. Arms differ by one environment variable on one machine; nothing here compares Loki to another vendor.
what_this_licenses: A hypothesis, and a reason to keep LOKI_SIMPLE=1 default-OFF. It does NOT license 'the stripped prompt is slower' as a claim. The overlap is real -- the simple arm produced three 1-iteration runs -- so the difference could still be run-to-run variance. Deciding it needs n where a 3-of-6 vs 0-of-6 split clears alpha, which is roughly n=8-10 per arm, or about 3 more hours of trials.
